Ruby 3.4.4, Rails 8.1.4, the gems of a default `rails new` app, SQLite, and Chromium are installed. You can install other gems from rubygems.org; other network access is blocked. Install all dependencies while you work: we verify the app without network access.

Feel free to store any design notes/insights that could be useful for future steps in the docs/ folder.

How we run the app:

- We start it with `bin/serve` from the project root and these environment variables: `RAILS_ENV=production`, `PORT=3000`, `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_USERNAME`, `QUIZZY_MODERATOR_PASSWORD`.
- `bin/serve` prepares everything the app needs (the database, assets, and so on) and runs the app in production mode in the foreground. It listens on all interfaces on `PORT`.
- The app is served over plain HTTP (no SSL, no HTTPS redirects) and accepts any host name.
- `GET /up` responds with `200` when the app is ready.
- The app keeps all its data under `storage/`. It must not call external services.

Our QA auto-tests drive the app in a browser and rely on the labels in quotes in each task. Keep them exactly as written, as visible text, a <label>, a placeholder, or an aria-label.

The QA auto-tests also expect:

- Each item of a list (a quiz, a question) sits in its own list item or table row, with its buttons and links inside it.
- Switches are checkboxes (a styled switch is fine if a real checkbox sits under it).
- Confirmations use the browser's native `confirm()` dialog.

Moderators started asking for this:

> As a moderator, I want to reuse my quiz at another conference, or share it with a colleague who runs Quizzy too.

The quiz page gets the "Export" link. It opens a page that shows the quiz as JSON inside a `<pre>` element (the only `<pre>` on the page), ready to copy.

`/moderate` gets the "Import quiz" button. It opens a page with a "Quiz JSON" text area and the "Import" button. Importing always creates a new quiz, even if a quiz with the same title exists, and opens its page.

The format:

```json
{
  "title": "Frontend Fest 2026",
  "questions": [
    {
      "text": "Which HTTP status code means \"Too Many Requests\"?",
      "active": true,
      "options": [
        {"text": "418", "correct": false},
        {"text": "429", "correct": true}
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `questions` and `options` keep their order.
- On import, `active` is optional (`true` by default), and `correct` is optional (`false` by default).
- The export always writes both, and it writes exactly these keys: the quiz title and its questions, nothing else. The export is only for moving quiz contents.
- Imported questions follow the same rules as the question form.

When the JSON is invalid or breaks a rule, the page shows an error and nothing is imported: not the quiz, not a part of its questions.

class Question < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :quiz
  has_many :options, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  scope :active, -> { where(active: true) }
  scope :ordered, -> { order(:position, :id) }

  validates :body, presence: true
  validates :position, presence: true, numericality: { only_integer: true, greater_than: 0 }

  def save_with_option_rows(body:, active:, option_rows:)
    trimmed_body = body.to_s.strip
    non_empty_rows = option_rows.reject { |row| row[:body].to_s.strip.blank? }

    form_errors = []
    form_errors << "Question can't be blank" if trimmed_body.blank?
    form_errors << "Add at least two options" if non_empty_rows.size < 2
    if non_empty_rows.any? && non_empty_rows.none? { |row| row[:correct] }
      form_errors << "Mark at least one option as correct"
    end

    return form_errors if form_errors.any?

    transaction do
      self.body = trimmed_body
      self.active = active
      self.position ||= (quiz.questions.maximum(:position) || 0) + 1
      save!

      options.destroy_all
      non_empty_rows.each_with_index do |row, index|
        options.create!(
          body: row[:body].to_s.strip,
          correct: row[:correct],
          position: index + 1
        )
      end
    end

    []
  end
end

class Quiz < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  before_validation :strip_title
  validates :title, presence: true

  def move_question_up!(question)
    move_question!(question, -1)
  end

  def move_question_down!(question)
    move_question!(question, 1)
  end

  private

  def strip_title
    self.title = title.to_s.strip
  end

  def move_question!(question, offset)
    transaction do
      ordered = questions.order(:position, :id).to_a
      idx = ordered.index(question)
      return unless idx

      target_idx = idx + offset
      return if target_idx < 0 || target_idx >= ordered.size

      ordered[idx], ordered[target_idx] = ordered[target_idx], ordered[idx]
      ordered.each_with_index do |q, i|
        q.update_column(:position, i + 1) if q.position != i + 1
      end
    end
  end
end

class Quiz < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :questions, -> { order(:position, :id) }, dependent: :destroy

  before_validation :strip_title
  validates :title, presence: true

  def move_question_up!(question)
    move_question!(question, -1)
  end

  def move_question_down!(question)
    move_question!(question, 1)
  end

  def export_payload
    {
      "title" => title,
      "questions" => questions.ordered.includes(:options).map do |question|
        {
          "text" => question.body,
          "active" => question.active?,
          "options" => question.options.map do |option|
            {
              "text" => option.body,
              "correct" => option.correct?
            }
          end
        }
      end
    }
  end

  def export_json
    JSON.pretty_generate(export_payload)
  end

  def self.import_from_json(raw_json)
    text = raw_json.to_s
    return [ nil, [ "Quiz JSON can't be blank" ] ] if text.strip.blank?

    begin
      data = JSON.parse(text)
    rescue JSON::ParserError => e
      return [ nil, [ "Invalid JSON: #{e.message}" ] ]
    end

    return [ nil, [ "Quiz JSON must be an object" ] ] unless data.is_a?(Hash)

    errors = []

    if !data.key?("title") || data["title"].nil?
      errors << "Title can't be blank"
    elsif !data["title"].is_a?(String)
      errors << "Title must be a string"
    elsif data["title"].strip.blank?
      errors << "Title can't be blank"
    end

    raw_questions = data["questions"]
    if !data.key?("questions") || !raw_questions.is_a?(Array)
      errors << "Questions must be an array"
    else
      raw_questions.each_with_index do |q_data, q_idx|
        q_num = q_idx + 1
        unless q_data.is_a?(Hash)
          errors << "Question #{q_num} must be an object"
          next
        end

        if !q_data.key?("text") || q_data["text"].nil?
          errors << "Question #{q_num}: Question can't be blank"
        elsif !q_data["text"].is_a?(String)
          errors << "Question #{q_num}: Question must be a string"
        elsif q_data["text"].strip.blank?
          errors << "Question #{q_num}: Question can't be blank"
        end

        if q_data.key?("active") && q_data["active"] != true && q_data["active"] != false
          errors << "Question #{q_num}: Active must be true or false"
        end

        raw_options = q_data["options"]
        unless raw_options.is_a?(Array)
          errors << "Question #{q_num}: Options must be an array"
          next
        end

        valid_options = []
        raw_options.each_with_index do |opt_data, o_idx|
          o_num = o_idx + 1
          unless opt_data.is_a?(Hash)
            errors << "Question #{q_num}, option #{o_num}: Option must be an object"
            next
          end

          if !opt_data.key?("text") || opt_data["text"].nil?
            errors << "Question #{q_num}, option #{o_num}: Option text can't be blank"
          elsif !opt_data["text"].is_a?(String)
            errors << "Question #{q_num}, option #{o_num}: Option text must be a string"
          elsif opt_data["text"].strip.blank?
            errors << "Question #{q_num}, option #{o_num}: Option text can't be blank"
          end

          correct_val = opt_data.key?("correct") ? opt_data["correct"] : false
          if correct_val != true && correct_val != false
            errors << "Question #{q_num}, option #{o_num}: Correct must be true or false"
          end

          valid_options << (correct_val == true)
        end

        if raw_options.size < 2
          errors << "Question #{q_num}: Add at least two options"
        elsif valid_options.any? && valid_options.none?
          errors << "Question #{q_num}: Mark at least one option as correct"
        end
      end
    end

    return [ nil, errors ] if errors.any?

    quiz = nil
    transaction do
      quiz = create!(title: data["title"].strip)
      raw_questions.each_with_index do |q_data, q_idx|
        active = q_data.key?("active") ? q_data["active"] : true
        question = quiz.questions.create!(
          body: q_data["text"].strip,
          active: active,
          position: q_idx + 1
        )
        q_data["options"].each_with_index do |opt_data, o_idx|
          correct = opt_data.key?("correct") ? opt_data["correct"] : false
          question.options.create!(
            body: opt_data["text"].strip,
            correct: correct,
            position: o_idx + 1
          )
        end
      end
    end

    [ quiz, [] ]
  end

  private

  def strip_title
    self.title = title.to_s.strip
  end

  def move_question!(question, offset)
    transaction do
      ordered = questions.order(:position, :id).to_a
      idx = ordered.index(question)
      return unless idx

      target_idx = idx + offset
      return if target_idx < 0 || target_idx >= ordered.size

      ordered[idx], ordered[target_idx] = ordered[target_idx], ordered[idx]
      ordered.each_with_index do |q, i|
        q.update_column(:position, i + 1) if q.position != i + 1
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF

    end
